title: P21: RMSNorm in place of LayerNorm
description: P21: replace all eight block LayerNorms and the final LayerNorm with learned-scale RMSNorm at epsilon 1e-5, preserving normalization placement throughout pretraining and downstream RL/evaluation. Retaining mean information in proof representations may improve exploration and adaptation under the fixed expert-iteration procedure.
hypothesis: No prior registration tests normalization type. Block sharing (014) and more heads (019) reduced downstream performance; EMA (025) improved short-proof greedy accuracy but hurt every downstream seed. RMS normalization preserves the residual mean instead of subtracting it, potentially retaining proof-state features useful beyond the initial length distribution. This is an unverified representation hypothesis. Standard RMSNorm also removes nine learned offsets (2304 parameters, 0.072%), so this does not isolate mean subtraction from affine-bias removal. Remaining initial parameters and RNG are unchanged. Only downstream three-seed dev-transfer performance decides keep/discard.
expected_delta: Central prediction +3 to +15 dev-transfer theorems at true length >=7 versus incumbent 012 (exact mean 147.67; stored rounded mean 148), with plausible downside -50. Seeds remain 0,1,2. Native RMSNorm may have different kernel efficiency on pinned PyTorch 2.4; estimate up to 20% slower pretraining and per-token inference, unmeasured on A40, with about 2400-3000 steps in 300 seconds. Learned generation lengths can further change runtime under the unchanged 1200-second cap.

arch.norm_affine: learned scale initialized to one; no offset
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: Construct fork GPT, replace all nine LayerNorms with torch.nn.RMSNorm(256, eps=1e-5), then load state. Live harness retains RMSNorm throughout RL.

config.init: Fork default normal std=0.02 for matrices; replace all nine LayerNorms after construction with unit-scale RMSNorm, preserving remaining parameters and RNG state.
